fantasy.injuryDetail: Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

Hockenson was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but it sounds like the tight end has a chance to return to practice after logging DNPs last week. In Hockenson's absence versus Green Bay in Week 10, fellow TE Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and a TD.

Evans missed the 49ers' last three games while recovering from right Achilles tendinitis, but he has a chance at returning to action in Week 11. After staying behind in the Bay Area this past weekend for the team's 46-40 win in Dallas, he's scheduled to meet back up with the 49ers this week in Colorado Springs, where the team will be holding practices at high altitude to get acclimated for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City. If Evans is able to practice in some capacity Wednesday through Friday and if his Achilles responds well, he'll likely be cleared to play for the first time since Week 6.

Even with the benefit of a Week 9 bye, Tate still wound up being sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on account of the shoulder injury. Though Saleh is optimistic that the rookie wideout will be ready to go for the Titans' upcoming game in Dallas, Tate will first need to return to practice in some fashion to make that a reality. Tate remained a non-participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep.

After their Week 10 bye, the Bears won't post their first Week 11 practice report until Wednesday, but Monangai may be trending toward being listed as a full participant. The second-year back was on the field for a second straight day Tuesday and didn't appear to be operating with any limitations while mixing into drills. Monangai had missed the Bears' previous five games due to turf toe and a right thumb injury, but he looks poised to return to action this Sunday against the Saints.

Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he still could be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.

Tennessee hasn't provided word on the severity of the ankle injury that Robinson sustained in the second half of this past Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars, but his move to IR ensures that he'll be sidelined for at least the next four games. While Robinson is out, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike should be locked into top-three roles at receiver alongside rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder), who has missed the past two contests but is expected back for a Week 11 matchup with Dallas. The Titans signed Xavier Restrepo off the practice squad to replace Robinson on the 53-man roster and bolster their depth at receiver.
out

Now that he's spent the required four games on IR while recovering from a finger injury, Wilson is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened this week. McCarthy expressed similar optimism that fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) will be able to come off IR this week, a development that could result in Wilson settling for a lesser role if both receivers are activated ahead of Sunday's contest. Despite a rough start to the season, Pittman signed a two-year, $35 million extension in March that likely affords him some security as a starter alongside DK Metcalf upon his return, which would leave Wilson to fend with rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart.
questionable

After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.
questionable

As a result of the transaction, the Commanders will have a 21-day window wherein they can evaluate Croskey-Merritt for a return to the 53-man roster. Depending on how he fares in practice during Week 11, Croskey-Merritt could be reinstated ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals. Whenever the Commanders elect to activate him, Croskey-Merritt will likely step back in as the team's lead runner, allowing Rachaad White to shift into more of a complementary role as the top pass-catching back.

After exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills to get checked for a concussion, Smith returned to the contest in the third quarter but then left the game for good after sustaining an ankle injury. Fortunately for Smith, he appears to have avoided a significant injury, but he'll still need to prove his health during Week 11 prep in order to play Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that Smith will remain the team's starter if healthy, but rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to direct the offense against the Chargers in the event Smith can't play.

Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

O'Connell indicated that Addison will be a candidate for injured reserve, though if he does end up being deactivated, the Vikings anticipate that the wideout would be able to return after sitting out the minimum four games. Addison injured his thumb at Friday's practice and subsequently was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay. For as long as Addison is sidelined, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton will be the options to see added reps behind No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

Marks sustained a concussion during Sunday's loss in Cleveland, and head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that the running back isn't likely to gain clearance to play Thursday versus the Colts, according to DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. The Texans may make a ruling on Marks' status as soon as they post Wednesday's injury report, and conversely position mate David Montgomery (groin) appears to be closing in on a return to action after logging a second full listing in a row going back to last week.

Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.

Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.
out

After missing Sunday's loss to the Browns, Harrison opened the new week with another missed practice due to his hamstring issue. If he's unable to return in time for Thursday night's game against the Colts on a short week, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell likely will soak up the vast majority of the snaps at wideout.

The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.
questionable

Mayfield sustained a foot sprain when he was sacked during the fourth quarter of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears, and he doesn't appear to have made a full recovery from the injury coming out of a Week 10 bye. After Mayfield was reportedly in and out of a walking boot throughout the bye week, the Buccaneers opted to make a couple of transactions Monday to stabilize their quarterback room. The Buccaneers will likely wait and see how Mayfield progresses during the week before making a call on his status for Sunday, but if he's unable to take any reps with the first-team offense during practice, Jalon Daniels would be in line to start in Detroit. Daniels previously went 1-2 as a starter while Mayfield was sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated right thumb.

Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but he now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If Shipley is able to suit up this weekend, he'll reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

Alie-Cox was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, and his groin injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. That means he'll be required to miss at least four games, and with the Colts on a bye for Week 13, that means the next time Alie-Cox can play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20. Will Mallory (hamstring) has also been ruled out for Week 10, so Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown will serve as the Colts' backup tight ends behind Tyler Warren against Miami.

Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

Mallory suffered a hamstring injury during Week 10 prep, and he was not cleared to play in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Indianapolis is operating on a short week, so Mallory faces an uphill battle to play against the Texans on Thursday.

Iosivas was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Steelers despite logging full practices Thursday and Friday. He'll remain on IR for at least one more game, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash. The wide receiver was listed as doubtful after Friday's third consecutive DNP, and it is no surprise that the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

Indianapolis has now estimated Gould as limited on both of its first two practice reports of Week 11, after he emerged from Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins with the toe injury. His status for Thursday's game against the Texans is muddled for the moment, but Gould could clear up any concern about his availability by turning in a full practice Wednesday. After Indianapolis shipped out two receivers (Keenan Allen and Josh Downs) at the trade deadline, Gould stepped in as the Colts' top option in the slot in Week 10 and finished with two receptions for 28 yards on four targets.

Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.
questionable

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter with an ankle injury. The tight end fractured his ankle and did not return to the contest. The 26-year-old will likely be placed on injured reserve soon, as he begins to recover from the injury.
questionable

Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.
Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.
